basics.name: Tomasz Frelek
basics.label: M.S. Student in Computer Science
basics.summary: A Master's student at UC San Diego with a background in Computer Science and Mathematics from The Ohio State University. Experienced in autonomous systems, computer vision, and machine learning. Passionate about developing perception systems for autonomous vehicles and applying machine learning to solve real-world challenges.

work.name: Oculii
work.summary: Internship focused on enhancing radar perception systems for autonomous vehicles.
highlights: Developed BEV transformer models for 3D object detection and semantic mapping, enhancing the perception system's MOTA score by 15%.
Engineered a modular model evaluation package for object detection models, accelerating feedback cycles 2X.
Engineered a synthetic data pipeline using CARLA and DSpace simulators to generate 100,000 frames of realistic radar data.
Contributed to CES preparations by developing tools for data synchronization and calibration.

work.name: The Ohio State University
work.summary: Research in Computer Vision for Ecological and Autonomous System Applications with Advisor Prof. Wei-Lun Chao.
highlights: Pioneering Imageomics applications, integrating machine learning and computer vision for biological data analysis.
Developing models for tasks such as species classification, trait labeling, and image segmentation.
Focusing on learning with few or imperfect data in autonomous driving by developing one/few-shot learning algorithms and leveraging synthetic data.

work.name: The Ohio State University
work.summary: Research in Time Series Classification and Forecasting with Advisor Prof. John Paparrizos.
highlights: Building a comprehensive library of 60+ time series classification algorithms with a unified interface.
Implementing and analyzing novel algorithms from cutting-edge research papers.
Utilizing PyTorch to develop, implement, and train deep-learning algorithms for time series classification.

work.name: JPMorgan Chase
work.summary: Two summer internships developing internal tools and data pipeline services.
highlights: Created an internal Python interface for Amazon S3, increasing data access speed by 50% for hundreds of development teams.
Developed a comprehensive health check application for a petabyte-scale data pipeline service using Java, SpringBoot, and React.
Leveraged CI/CD frameworks like Jenkins and Maven to streamline application development and deployment.
Collaborated with dozens of teams using Agile principles and Git on an interface utilized by 500+ developers.

club.summary: Collaborated on a team to build a SAE Level 4 autonomous vehicle for urban driving competitions.
highlights: Developed and integrated perception algorithms for real-time object detection, classification, and tracking using LIDAR and camera data.
Designed and implemented deep learning models using PyTorch for pedestrian detection and semantic segmentation, achieving 90% accuracy in trials.

club.summary: Managed club finances and organized major events to promote AI on campus.
highlights: Managed over $10,000 in club finances and sponsorships.
Organized 'HackAI', an AI-focused hackathon with over 150 participants.
Developed and led a machine learning project series teaching scikit-learn and OpenCV.
Organized a university-wide AI research expo connecting 100+ students with 15+ faculty presenters.

projects.name: NASA Airport Throughput Prediction Challenge
projects.summary: Collaborated on a small team to develop a regression model to forecast airport throughput for U.S. airports.
highlights: Achieved 9th place out of 53 teams with 78.77% accuracy.
Constructed a comprehensive data pipeline to automate data extraction, feature engineering, training, and prediction.
Processed and analyzed over 200 GB of flight and weather data (FUSER, METAR, TAF, CWAM).
Used deep-learning (LSTM) and machine-learning (LightGBM) frameworks to develop the time series model.

projects.name: CVPR 2025 Anti-UAV Challenge
projects.summary: Developed an anti-UAV (drone) tracking and detection system for a CVPR workshop challenge.
highlights: Adapted and trained SiamFC for object tracking and YOLOv11 for object detection.
Engineered a custom data pipeline to subsample a large-scale dataset for model compatibility.
Evaluated model performance using metrics such as mean IoU, success rate, and mAP50.
